articles.title: “I regretted the way I acted toward..”: How Patrick Mahomes' $50,000 NFL fine after Travis Kelce's wiped-out touchdown sparks the Kansas City Chiefs controversy
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes rarely loses his cool on the football field, but the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback struggled to hide his frustration after a
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes rarely loses his cool on the football field, but the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback struggled to hide his frustration after a controversial call against the Buffalo Bills in December 2023. A spectacular play involving Travis Kelce appeared to give Kansas City a late lead before officials stepped in. What followed was an angry sideline outburst, a public apology and a $50,000 fine from the NFL.The December 10 clash at Arrowhead Stadium ended in a 20-17 defeat for the Chiefs. However, the result was soon overshadowed by the disputed touchdown and Mahomes' reaction. Travis Kelce had produced one of the most creative plays of the season, but Kadarius Toney's penalty turned the moment into a major talking point across the league. Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce's incredible touchdown turns into Chiefs' costly controversyKansas City needed a big play against Buffalo, and Patrick Mahomes appeared to find the answer with just over a minute remaining. The quarterback connected with Kelce for a 25-yard completion. The tight end then spotted Toney and threw a 24-yard lateral across the field, allowing the receiver to run into the end zone.It looked like a brilliant go-ahead touchdown. However, officials had already thrown a flag for offensive offsides against Toney. His position over the line of scrimmage before the snap wiped out the score.Mahomes was furious. He shouted toward the officials, slammed his helmet and later confronted Bills quarterback Josh Allen after the game. During his postgame comments, Mahomes questioned the decision and said the call had taken away a special moment for Kelce."It's tough to swallow," Mahomes told reporters after the 20-17 loss. He also argued that fans wanted players on the field to decide games rather than see a late flag change the outcome.Kelce later explained the play with his brother Jason on their December 13, 2023, episode of the New Heights podcast. The Chiefs tight end admitted he had never thrown a lateral that far."When it left my hand, I thought it got tipped," Kelce said while recalling the moment. He also revealed that the pass came close to being intercepted, making the ambitious decision even riskier.Despite the disappointment, Kelce stood by Toney. On the same podcast, he recalled telling his teammate, "Hey, man, we're just gonna have to do it again, big dog." He also defended the receiver against the criticism that followed the penalty.Patrick Mahomes admits his mistake before NFL hands Chiefs QB a $50,000 fineThe controversy did not end with the final whistle. A day after the loss, Patrick Mahomes appeared on The Drive on 610 Sports Radio on December 11, 2023, and admitted that his reaction had gone too far."Obviously, you don't want to react that way," Patrick Mahomes said during the interview. He explained that his frustration came from wanting to win and supporting his teammates, but acknowledged that he should not have directed his anger at officials.His biggest regret, however, involved Allen."More than anything, I regretted the way I acted toward Josh after the game because he had nothing to do with it," Mahomes admitted. He also called his behaviour "not a great example for kids watching the game."The NFL soon handed down its punishment. Mahomes received a $50,000 fine for his criticism of the officials and unsportsmanlike conduct. Head coach Andy Reid also faced a $100,000 fine for publicly criticising the officiating.NFL commissioner Roger Goodell backed the decision during the league's owners' meeting in Irving, Texas, on December 13. He said the officials had made "absolutely the right call."The Chiefs had every reason to feel frustrated, but the league stood by its officials. Toney had lined up illegally, and the penalty followed the rules.For Mahomes, the incident became an unusual moment of public frustration. For Kelce, it was a remarkable piece of improvisation that never made the official highlight reel as a touchdown. Their connection produced the play, but the penalty and the fallout made it one of the most talked-about Chiefs moments of the 2023 season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How much will Josh Downs play in Chiefs debut? Kansas City's plans for new WR raise intrigue
articles.summary: Josh Downs is expected to make his Kansas City Chiefs debut against the Atlanta Falcons, but his arrival does not automatically mean a major increase in
articles.body: Josh Downs is expected to make his Kansas City Chiefs debut against the Atlanta Falcons, but his arrival does not automatically mean a major increase in the team's receiving production. Kansas City acquired the former Indianapolis Colts wideout before the trade deadline to address a passing game that has struggled for consistency. However, with only a few days to learn Andy Reid's offense, Downs faces a different challenge. The Chiefs need his ability to create separation, but they also have reasons to introduce him gradually rather than hand him an immediate starting role.Josh Downs could have a limited role in his first Chiefs appearanceKansas City has reasons to be excited about Downs, particularly after its recent offensive struggles. His ability to beat defenders in tight coverage gives Patrick Mahomes another option underneath, something the Chiefs have not always managed to establish consistently this season. Still, expecting an immediate connection between the new receiver and his quarterback would be premature.Downs has had little time to absorb Reid's playbook. Learning the terminology is one thing, but understanding the timing, adjustments and responsibilities behind each route takes considerably longer. The Chiefs cannot afford to put him into situations where a missed assignment could disrupt an entire play.There is also the question of how Kansas City plans to distribute its snaps. Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy remain important pieces of the receiving group, while Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen are also competing for opportunities. Worthy is working his way back from a hamstring injury, but his availability gives Reid another reason not to overload Downs immediately.His size could also influence the plan. Listed at 5-foot-9 and 171 pounds, Downs is better suited to a specialised role than an every-down workload. Across nine games with Indianapolis, he recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and one touchdown. Those numbers do not tell the whole story, though. His value comes largely from his ability to separate from defenders, especially in man coverage, rather than stretching the field for explosive gains.Third downs could be where Kansas City gets the most from Josh DownsThe most sensible way to use Downs against Atlanta may be through short routes and third-down situations. His quickness and route-running skills can give Mahomes a reliable option when the defence tightens its coverage. He does not need 10 or 12 targets to make an impact. A handful of well-timed receptions could show why Kansas City wanted him in the first place.Kenneth Walker's absence could push the Chiefs towards a more pass-heavy approach, but that does not necessarily mean Downs will receive a large share of the opportunities. Reid still has to balance the available personnel and avoid asking a newcomer to handle assignments he has barely practised.Kansas City's recent trade history also offers a reason for patience. Kadarius Toney, Mecole Hardman and DeAndre Hopkins all finished their first games after arriving at the trade deadline with no more than two catches or 30 receiving yards. That history does not guarantee a quiet debut for Downs, but it does show how difficult an immediate adjustment can be.If Downs gets only a few opportunities against Atlanta, it should not be viewed as a failed start. His bigger test will come as he learns the system and builds timing with Mahomes. Kansas City needs another dependable receiver, not a rushed debut.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after suffering a "significant" knee injury during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots, according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that it is a "significant" injury.

Hutchinson was hurt when he landed awkwardly after celebrating a sack on New England's opening drive of the first quarter.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport described Hutchinson as doing a "full Gramatica." Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made field goal in a 2001 game.

Hutchinson enjoyed a return to form in 2025 after fractures to his tibia and fibula limited him to five games a season earlier. He had 14.5 sacks en route to earning a second Pro Bowl nod and finishing fifth in the Defensive Player of the Year voting.

The fifth-year pass-rusher was delivering more of the same through the Lions' first eight games. He had five sacks and 18 hits on the quarterback, and he made his presence felt early Sunday by bringing down Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

Entering Week 10, Detroit was allowing 355 yards per game, which is tied for 26th, and ranks last in pass defense (260.9). That's despite totaling the third-most sacks (27) in the NFL.

Losing Hutchinson for any period of time would be a massive blow for the unit.

articles.title: Rex Ryan declines to address alleged hit-and-run during ESPN's 'Sunday NFL Countdown'
articles.summary: The former Jets and Bills head coach faces six misdemeanor charges following his arrest in Nashville.
articles.body:
Rex Ryan restricted his time on ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown" to talking about football this week, rather than his hit-and-run arrest in Nashville four days ago .

The former New York Jets head coach declined to address his alleged incident on Nov. 4 while appearing on the air, continuing a lack of comment since his arrest on Wednesday. It was reported by multiple outlets Saturday evening that Ryan and ESPN were planning for him to work as usual, and that he wasn't expected to discuss the arrest.

When it came time for Ryan to make his appearance, he was ready to talk about the early injuries in the Detroit Lions-New England Patriots game in Germany.

The alleged incident occurred on Nashville's famous Broadway Street, with Ryan accused of turning at an intersection while two pedestrians had a walk sign. He allegedly ran his truck over both victims' feet and made contact with one of their legs, then continued to drive. He was allegedly confronted by the victims at a subsequent red light and argued with them before driving off, but not before the victims took a picture of his "HIT QBS" vanity license plate.

One of the victims, Michael Holland, later identified himself to the New York Post and said the other victim was his wife. He shared further details about the incident and aftermath, including a picture of his wife's bruised leg. He said his wife has already lost a toenail and he expects to lose two as well. He also said he plans to undergo X-rays on his feet soon.

He also recalled his confrontation with Ryan:

Holland claimed that he pounded on Ryan's window and the ESPN analyst then "got out and confronted us." "He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done," Holland said of their encounter, "and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, 'Sorry,' he just got back in his vehicle and took off."

Holland claimed that he pounded on Ryan's window and the ESPN analyst then "got out and confronted us."

"He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done," Holland said of their encounter, "and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, 'Sorry,' he just got back in his vehicle and took off."

Ryan's attorney reportedly declined comment on the allegations when reached by the Post. ESPN responded Wednesday with a confirmation they were "aware" of the allegations.

The incident was reportedly caught on camera, with footage later reviewed by the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department. Ryan turned himself in to law enforcement on Wednesday and was released on $6,000 bond, with his next hearing scheduled for Dec. 18.

Ryan faces six misdemeanor charges stemming from the incident: two counts each of leaving the scene of an accident, failure to give information or render aid and failure to obey a traffic control signal.

Ryan has worked as an analyst for ESPN since 2017, following a lengthy coaching career in which he accrued a 61-66 record as head coach for the Jets and Buffalo Bills.

This isn't his first known car accident, as he avoided injury and arrest after allegedly causing a three-car accident by running a red light in Pennsylvania in 2013 during his time with the Jets . He received a written warning, but no citation.

articles.body:
New England Patriots star receiver A.J. Brown picked up another injury in Sunday's NFL Munich Game against the Detroit Lions.

Brown was seen heading to the locker room in the fourth quarter, and the Patriots later announced that he is out for the remainder of the game due to a hamstring injury. He was initially deemed questionable to return.

Brown caught two of his six targets for 27 yards before exiting the game. He had a stint on injured reserve earlier this year after suffering a sprained ankle in Week 1, and he missed more time after picking up a knee injury before returning for Sunday's matchup against the Lions.

This new injury continues a year of disappointment for Brown after he forced his way off the Philadelphia Eagles over the offseason. In his three appearances before Sunday's game, he produced just nine catches for 101 yards and no touchdowns, a far cry from what the Patriots expected when they gave up a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to acquire him.

In addition to Brown's injury on Sunday, the Patriots also lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury in the first quarter. He was seen limping back to the locker room, leaving backup Tommy DeVito to take over.

The Patriots were hoping to contend for a second straight trip to the Super Bowl, but their chances are looking slim as the injuries start to pile up. The team will be hoping that Brown and Maye won't have to miss too much time as they try to remain in the hunt for the postseason.

articles.title: NFL: Detorit Lions thump New England Patriots in Germany after Drake Maye injury as Amon-Ra St Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs star
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs posts 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns while the New England Patriots lose quarterback Drake Maye to injury on the opening drive of the game; the Detroit Lions emerge 35-10 winners at the Allianz Arena in Munich in the NFL's eighth of nine international games in 2026
articles.body:
Gibbs finished with 252 yards and two touchdowns from scrimmage, including 153 rushing yards and 99 through the air, while St Brown - born to a German mother - recorded four catches for 98 yards and two scores to reward his hero's welcome in Europe.

New England's offense capitulated after the opening drive of the game when Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury before being replaced by Tommy DeVito at quarterback.

DeVito struggled to move the ball as he finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while being sacked four times. Lions quarterback Jared Goff was 20 of 31 for 303 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.

It marked the penultimate game of a record nine international matchups in 2026 as the league prepares to conclude its road-trip in Mexico City next Sunday.

The result lifted Detroit to 7-2 on the year amid their Super Bowl charge, while dropping the Patriots to 5-5 as they continue their bid to swerve a hangover from February's season-finale loss to Seattle.

The Patriots lost Maye to injury on the opening drive when he landed awkwardly during a drive-ending sack from Aidan Hutchinson, which saw Andy Borregales kick a 33-yard field goal.

Lions edge rusher Hutchinson also limped off in the aftermath of the play, having injured his knee while celebrating the sack, with his ailment feared to be significant enough to keep him out for the season, according to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport.

The German-speaking St Brown, whose mother is from Leverkusen, then put Detroit in control with a 56-yard touchdown catch-and-run to mark his emotional homecoming.

St Brown's mother Miriam would take her son and his brothers back to Germany to see their grandparents each summer during their childhood, with the Lions receiver having represented the German national team in the sophomore year of high school and sat his SATs in English, German and French. St Brown has also returned to Germany regularly to host football camps, and wears the German flag on his helmet.

The Lions bolstered their advantage through a 12-yard touchdown catch from Isaac TesLaa, who swivelled his hips superbly to make a back-peddling snag for 14-3.

New England sought to claw their way back when Christian Gonzalez intercepted Goff on third-and-nine with six minutes to play in the first half, only for a subsequent three-and-out to sum up the struggles they would face on offense for the rest of the game.

Kevin Byard kept the Lions alive at the end of the first half when he broke up a pass to Sam LaPorta for a would-be touchdown, before intercepted Goff in the end zone on the very next play.

St Brown added his second in the third quarter when he bundled over for a 28-yard touchdown with some help from his ploughing offensive lineman, giving the Lions a 28-3 advantage. The celebration was... interesting, the Lions dropping on all fours and crawling like a... human centipede? St Brown had promised a nod to Germany during the week were he to find the end zone; this was probably it. Dare we say more?

Mike Vrabel's injury list extended in the second half when AJ Brown limped to the locker room with a hamstring injury at the start of the fourth quarter in the latest disruption to his first season with the Patriots.

The Patriots found the end zone for the first time moments later when DeVito fired a 10-yard touchdown pass to second-year undrafted running back Lan Larison.

Detroit replied immediately and emphatically when Penei Sewell's blocking exploits paved the way for Gibbs to strike again with a 28-yard touchdown run to build on his mammoth performance, taking him over 250 scrimmage yards for the day.

"It's been probably one of the most fun days I've ever had. Playing for Detroit, being in Germany with these fans, coming out with a win like this - it's been amazing.

"I'm sad to leave, but it was a really fun three days.

"I feel like we could have scored more points than we did today - that's being a bit greedy, but we had a lot of three-and-outs.

"When we did get going we got going, which was good, but I still think we can be better."

articles.summary: The Detroit Lions continue to roll.
articles.body:
Detroit defeated the New England Patriots 35-10 in Sunday's showdown at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, to extend its winning streak to five as it improved to 7-2 on the season. As for the 5-5 Patriots, they have now lost three of their last four and have bigger concerns after ruling out quarterback Drake Maye out with an ankle injury he suffered in the first quarter.

That put Tommy DeVito under center, and he couldn't keep pace with Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and the rest of the Lions' offensive firepower. Gibbs in particular was unstoppable, while both he and St. Brown scored multiple touchdowns.

Rules Experts: Maye Sack Not Hip-Drop Tackle

Sunday's game started in problematic fashion for both teams, as both Maye and Lions pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson went to the locker room. Hutchinson's setback was ruled a knee injury and appeared to happen as he was celebrating a sack:

Even without Hutchinson, the Lions still seized full control in the first half.

St. Brown broke free in the New England secondary for a 56-yard score as the game's first touchdown before Goff found Isaac TeSlaa for another touchdown to open up a two-score advantage. TeSlaa's touchdown was the final play of a 97-yard drive that featured plenty of Gibbs cutting his way into space and using his speed to blow past defenders.

It was fitting, then, when he scored the next touchdown shortly before halftime to put New England in a daunting 21-3 hole with its backup quarterback playing.

It wasn't all good news for the Detroit offense, as Goff threw interceptions to Christian Gonzalez and Kevin Byard in the first half. The Byard pick came in the end zone and at least kept the AFC East team somewhat within striking distance heading into the second half.

But striking distance with DeVito is different than it would have been with Maye.

The backup threw an interception to Roger McCreary in the first half and continued to struggle against the Lions defense after intermission. Even with A.J. Brown back in the lineup for the first time since Oct. 22, New England struggled to get anything going with Maye sidelined.

By the time St. Brown used his physicality to power his way into the end zone for his second touchdown, the game was all but over. It was also fitting that St. Brown played so well in Germany, as he spent significant time growing up in the country where his mother, Miriam, was born.

To DeVito's credit, he fought through the early struggles and directed an impressive 13-play, 87-yard touchdown drive that he finished in the fourth quarter with a connection to Lan Larison for the running back's first career touchdown.

Yet even that drive featured a concern, as Brown went to the locker room with a hamstring injury and was ruled out .

Gibbs added insult to injury with another long touchdown run as the fourth quarter continued, giving the Lions plenty of momentum as they turn their attention to a home game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

As for the Patriots, they at least have a bye week as they deal with a number of high-profile injuries.

articles.body:
Your final--Browns 27, Texans 24. The Browns are 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963.

To be clear, the Browns are a flawed team. They commit too many penalties. They allow too many sacks. The run game is erratic on a good day.

But exactly zero people expected this Browns team to be 6-4 10 games in. Vegas didn't expect Cleveland to win six games period.

When the Browns went down 17, it would have been easy to roll over. It's what most would have expected from the Browns before the season.

But this Browns team doesn't quit. The defense was lights-out after halftime. Deshaun Watson threw for 300-plus yards for the third straight game--a feat he last accomplished in 2020.

The Browns are an impressive 6-2 in one-score games this year. Todd Monken deserves Coach of the Year consideration.

articles.title: Rex Ryan Is Back on ESPN Days After Arrest in Nashville
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Former NFL coach Rex Ryan was back in his role as ESPN analyst on Sunday, a few days after his arrest.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Former NFL coach Rex Ryan was back in his role as ESPN analyst on Sunday, a few days after his arrest.

Ryan turned himself in to Nashville police on Wednesday on misdemeanor charges after he allegedly hit two pedestrians with his truck in a popular area downtown last week and then drove off after an argument, police said.

The former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach was in ESPN's studio for its three-hour "NFL Sunday Countdown" pregame show. Ryan didn't address his arrest.

Ryan was driving a pickup truck when he allegedly ran over the feet of both individuals, who had the right of way crossing a main street in Nashville's honky-tonk and music tourist district on Nov. 5, police said in a release Wednesday.

The pedestrians involved, who sustained minor injuries, waved Ryan down at another red light and said he stepped out to argue with them, according to police. They took a photo of the driver and the truck's license plate, police said.

Ryan "immediately surrendered" himself to authorities after learning of the charges, his attorney, David Raybin, said Wednesday.

"From the outset, Coach Ryan has been fully cooperative with law enforcement and he intends to remain cooperative as the case moves forward," Raybin said. "Because we just received the warrant today, we currently have limited information regarding the allegations."

Ryan was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information or render aid and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal, according to court records. All are misdemeanors.

A judicial commissioner set Ryan's bond at $6,000, but he qualified for pretrial release, according to the Davidson County Sheriff's Office. That means he was released on non-financial conditions. He is scheduled to appear in court next month.

Ryan led the Jets to the AFC championship game in consecutive years after the 2009 and 2010 seasons.

While with the Jets, Ryan became one of the team's — and the NFL's — most popular figures, especially during his first few seasons as coach, because of his brash, colorful approach in news conferences that became must-watch TV.

He has not coached since being fired by the Bills with one game left in the 2016 season, though he has since expressed an interest in coaching and interviewed in 2025 for the Jets' head coaching vacancy when Aaron Glenn was hired.

His father, the late Buddy Ryan, was an NFL coaching legend who famously coordinated the 1985 Chicago Bears defense that was one of the best in history. Seth Ryan, one of Rex Ryan's two sons, is currently in his first season as the Jets' passing game coordinator.

Ryan is best known now for his work at ESPN as one of the analysts on the network's NFL pregame show.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Injured, Latest on Chiefs TE's Status After Exiting to Locker Room vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce was able to return after leaving the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons with an ankle injury.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce was able to return after leaving the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons with an ankle injury.

The team previously announced he was questionable to return.

The future Hall of Famer went to the locker room with the setback.

Kelce has been one of the most durable players in the NFL over the past decade. His only absence due to an injury since 2014 was in Week 1 of the 2023 season against the Detroit Lions when he had a knee bruise.

Even as Kelce has reached his mid-30s and his overall performance has shown signs of decline, he's in the starting lineup every week. His presence was extremely valuable for the Chiefs during the 2024 season while they navigated injuries and struggles among their receiver room.

The Chiefs' pass-catching group is still a question this season, with Kelce and Rashee Rice the only proven options. Tyquan Thornton had given them a downfield threat, but a dislocated ankle suffered in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders will likely keep him for most of the season.

Losing Kelce for any length of time would be devastating for a Chiefs offense because of his reliability and connection with Patrick Mahomes, who is recovering from a torn ACL suffered late last season.

Kelce doesn't take over games like he once did, but he's still Mahomes' favorite target. He currently leads the team in targets, receptions and yards.

The good news is Kansas City's offense has been phenomenal because the addition of Kenneth Walker III in free agency has reignited the running game, taking pressure off Mahomes and the passing attack.

However, Walker was also out for the game against the Vikings.

Kansas City will turn to backup tight end Noah Gray with Kelce out of the lineup. Gray knows this offense very well having played with the club for six seasons. He had a career-high 437 receiving yards in 2024.

articles.title: How Josh Allen is building his business empire beyond the NFL with Out of Pocket Studios, his $330 million Bills contract and New Era investment
articles.summary: Josh Allen is building a career beyond football, and his biggest business move so far is Out of Pocket Studios, a media company he launched on September
articles.body: Josh Allen is building a career beyond football, and his biggest business move so far is Out of Pocket Studios, a media company he launched on September 1, 2026. The Buffalo Bills quarterback is not just the face of the company. He serves as its CEO and executive producer, giving him a direct role in choosing and developing projects that could grow into a business beyond his NFL career.Josh Allen’s Out of Pocket Studios and his plans to build a media businessOut of Pocket Studios is focused on entertainment, advertising and live experiences. In simple terms, the company wants to create television shows, documentaries, comedy projects and other content that can reach audiences through different platforms. What makes this business interesting is that Allen is taking an active part in its development instead of simply allowing a company to use his name for promotion.The studio has backing from Skydance Sports, the sports production arm of Skydance. This gives Allen access to people and resources that can help turn his ideas into finished projects. Lindsey Cohen serves as the company’s president of strategy and operations, while Allen leads it as CEO and works as an executive producer.The company also had several projects ready around its launch. One of them was America’s Tailgate, a television special that aired on CBS during Labor Day weekend in 2026. Hosted by Nate Burleson and Melanie Collins, the programme brought together football, celebrities and entertainment.Another project is NFL Play Action, a weekly football show hosted by Kyle Brandt and Ally Love. It began streaming on Paramount+ on September 9, 2026, with 13 episodes planned. The show looks at football from different angles, including the biggest matchups, players and the culture around the NFL. Allen is among its executive producers.The studio is also working on The Buffalo Miracle, a documentary about a McDonald’s manager who opened the restaurant to help people stranded during Buffalo’s deadly Christmas Eve blizzard in 2022. A comedy series based on an idea from Allen has also reportedly found a buyer.These projects give the company different ways to make money. Television and streaming deals, advertising, sponsorships and production partnerships can all bring in revenue. However, there are no publicly confirmed figures showing how much Out of Pocket Studios has earned so far. Its ownership structure, valuation and exact funding amount have also not been disclosed.Josh Allen’s $330 million NFL contract, new era investment and business earningsAllen’s football career gives him a strong financial base to explore business opportunities. In March 2025, he signed a six-year contract extension with the Buffalo Bills worth $330 million, including $250 million in guaranteed money. The deal set a new NFL record for guaranteed money at the time, making it one of the biggest contracts in the league.His earnings are not limited to his NFL salary. Forbes ranked Allen second on its 2026 list of the highest-paid NFL players, estimating his total earnings at $73 million. The figure includes his football income and money from activities outside the sport. Forbes also listed several major brands connected to him, including New Balance, New Era, PepsiCo, Delta Air Lines and Pizza Hut.Another important business move came in July 2025, when Allen expanded his partnership with New Era Cap. Instead of remaining only a brand ambassador, he received an investment stake in the company and was given the title of its first-ever Director of Billustration.The partnership also had a connection to the Buffalo community. Allen worked with New Era on special caps designed with the help of young patients at Oishei Children’s Hospital. He wore the caps during Bills home-game arrivals, with the proceeds from their auctions supporting the Patricia Allen Fund.New Era confirmed that Allen became the first brand ambassador to receive an investment stake in the company. However, neither side revealed the size of his share or its financial value.There is also an important difference between Allen’s two business roles. His New Era partnership gives him an ownership interest in an existing brand, while Out of Pocket Studios is a company he leads as CEO and helps develop through his work as an executive producer.It is still too early to know how successful the media company will become financially. Allen has not shared how much personal money he has invested, and there are no confirmed figures for its profits or valuation. Still, his involvement in several projects and his partnership with Skydance Sports give the company a starting point in the entertainment business.For Allen, the idea is to create something that can continue to grow even when his playing days are over. Rather than depending only on his football career and advertising deals, he now has a chance to develop original shows and stories under his own company’s name.How Josh Allen Is Building a Business Career That Can Last Beyond His NFL DaysOut of Pocket Studios gives Allen a chance to work in entertainment while using his experience and popularity as an NFL star. His role as CEO and executive producer also means he can take part in developing projects instead of simply promoting them.With Skydance Sports supporting the company and several projects already in progress, Allen is trying to build a business that can stand on its own beyond his playing career.Josh Allen's move into business shows that he is thinking about his future beyond the NFL. articles.title: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson feared to have suffered season-ending knee injury celebrating sack of Drake Maye
articles.summary: Aidan Hutchinson leapt into the air after a sack and came down hard.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson made his presence known early against the New England Patriots. On the Patriots' first offensive drive, Hutchinson broke through the line on third down and sacked Drake Maye.

Following the play, Hutchinson got up to celebrate the sack. He jumped into the air and immediately fell to the ground after landing. Hutchinson appeared to be holding his right knee.

Hutchinson walked off the field, but headed straight to the medical tent on the sideline. He was later spotted on the broadcast heading to the locker room.

He was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury, but late in the third quarter, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Detroit eventually cruised to a 35-10 victory .

Early reports suggested Hutchinson may have sustained a "significant" knee injury, per NFL Network. Detroit is reportedly not expecting good news. While a second opinion is coming, it's possible Hutchinson will not return this season.

"We'll know more when we get back in the States," head coach Dan Campbell said postgame, according to the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi . "Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy."

Hutchinson wasn't the only player injured on the play. Maye also left the game . He was deemed questionable to return due to an ankle injury before eventually also being ruled out.

Losing Hutchinson for any significant period of time would be a devastating result for the Lions. Coming into the game, Hutchinson was Pro Football Focus' top-graded edge rusher on the year.

While NFL players rarely get injured while celebrating plays, it has happened before. Famously in 2001, Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL after celebrating a first quarter field goal in a game against the New York Giants.

articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson's Hit on Drake Maye That Injured Patriots QB Addressed by NFL Rules Expert
articles.summary: The New England Patriots' disappointing season took a nightmarish turn during Sunday's 35-10 loss against the Detroit Lions in Munich.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots' disappointing season took a nightmarish turn during Sunday's 35-10 loss against the Detroit Lions in Munich.

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered an injury early in the first quarter after being sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson on third down. Despite an outcry from fans, Fox Sports rule analyst Mike Pereira said during the broadcast that Hutchinson's sack was "not a hip-drop" tackle, per ESPN's Mike Reiss .

"Three things have to happen: You have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee," Pereira said. "This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse-collar penalty."

NFL officiating analyst Walt Anderson confirmed Pereira's explanation through a league spokesman, Reiss reported. Anderson noted that the sack did not qualify as a hip-drop tackle because there was no swivel or unweighting. It also did not qualify as a horse collar tackle because Hutchinson did not grab Maye's collar or nameplate.

Hutchinson reached around Maye's right shoulder pad and landed on Maye's lower leg as he brought him down. The third-year quarterback limped to the sideline before returning to the locker room for further evaluation.

Hutchinson celebrated the sack with his typical leap in the air, but he landed awkwardly and injured his right knee.

Both Maye and Hutchinson were ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Patriots backup quarterback Tommy DeVito wasn't able to find much production with New England's injury-riddled offensive unit. He completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

The Patriots will head into their much-needed bye week with a 5-5 record and a long flight home.

articles.title: Jets Lose to Bills Amid Geno Smith Injury, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Klubnik, Allen, More
articles.summary: The New York Jets suffered a 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills, but they may have incurred an even bigger blow.
articles.body:
The New York Jets suffered a 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills, but they may have incurred an even bigger blow.

Jets rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik got his first taste of NFL action after starter Geno Smith suffered multiple injuries.

Week 10 Fantasy Injury Report and Last Minute Waiver Wire Replacements

Klubnik entered the game to start the second half while starter Smith was being evaluated for a concussion, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo . He subsequently cleared protocol and re-entered the game in the third.

Smith played one series and took another big hit at the end of the drive, forcing Klubnik to return to the game once again. The veteran was initially deemed questionable to return due to an ankle injury, and he went back to the locker room to be evaluated further before being ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Smith was initially injured on a big hit near the end of the first half, as two Bills defenders hit him high and low as he fired an incomplete pass into the end zone, forcing the Jets to settle for a field goal.

Klubnik had a few big moments in his first series, completing two of his four passes for 39 yards and rushing for 19 yards to help lead New York into the red zone. However, the team failed to convert on third down once again, forcing kicker Jason Sanders to kick his third field goal of the day.

On the ensuing possession, the Bills marched right down the field, with star quarterback Josh Allen finding tight end Dalton Kincaid for a 54-yard catch-and-run. Allen punched it in for his second rushing touchdown of the day. The Bills quickly pulled away, with star running back James Cook capping things off with a 74-yard touchdown run.

After falling to 2-8, the Jets are likely headed for their 16th straight year without a playoff appearance. While Smith gives New York its best chance to win if he's healthy, the team will likely give Klubnik a chance to show what he has later in the year.

articles.title: Titans kicker Joey Slye delivers hit of the week that levels Jaguars returner, forces fumble
articles.summary: Kickers are football players too.
articles.body:
Take, for instance, Tennessee Titans kicker Joey Slye.

The Tennessee Titans kicker had an opportunity on Sunday to make a play outside the confines of his typical duties against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Following a third-quarter field goal that cut Jacksonville's lead to 16-13, Slye kicked the ball off to Jacksonville return man Josh Cameron.

Cameron fielded the kick inside the 5-yard line and returned it up the middle past the 30. When he got there, Slye was waiting.

Slye had sprinted up the field in return coverage and had a clear, head-on look at a play on Cameron. He delivered with a crunching blow that would have made any NFL linebacker proud.

The hit forced a fumble from Cameron. Unfortunately for the Titans, they didn't recover it, and the Jaguars converted their recovery into a 71-yard touchdown drive.

But Slye's impact on the play and the game was seen. At 228 pounds, Slye could be mistaken at a glance for an NFL linebacker. His primary job, of course, is not to deliver hits, but kick the ball.

And he did that with great success Sunday, sending each of his three field-goal attempts through the uprights. Each of those kicks was from 50-plus yards, with his longest coming from 54.

Unfortunately for the Titans, the Jaguars countered with four made field goals from Cam Little in addition to four touchdowns, three of them thrown by quarterback Trevor Lawrence.

articles.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Talks 'Dream Come True' After Lions' Rout of Patriots in NFL Germany Game

Amon-Ra St. Brown had the chance to play an NFL game in his mother's homeland, and he called it an experience he'll "never forget."

St. Brown, who speaks German, came out of the tunnel at Allianz Arena waving a German flag.

He proceeded to guide the Lions to a win as he caught four passes for 98 yards and a pair of touchdowns.

Playing in Germany was surely special for everyone involved, but it might have meant a bit more to St. Brown. The trip was made even sweeter after the Lions won their fifth game in a row to improve to 7-2.

articles.title: Cousins Beats Packers in Vikings Return, Box Score Stats & Highlights for JJettas, Love, Top Players
articles.summary: In his return to Minnesota, Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings handed Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers an 30-10 loss on Sunday.
articles.body:
In his return to Minnesota, Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings handed Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers an 30-10 loss on Sunday.

Cousins suited up in black and purple for the first time since the 2023-24 season, after spending six years in Minnesota. He then spent two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before joining the Las Vegas Raiders, where he played nine games this season.

Cousins was traded to Minnesota on Tuesday for a 2027 third-round draft pick, per ESPN's Ian Rapoport, making way for last year's Heisman Trophy winner, Fernando Mendoza, in Las Vegas.

The Vikings entered the matchup as 2.5-point underdogs against the Packers at Lambeau Field, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but pulled off the upset to snap a two-game losing streak.

In his first game back for the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns to lead the Vikings to their first win since Oct. 25. Minnesota had lost its previous two games against the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills.

1. DET: 7-2 (OVR), 2-0 (DIV), 4-1 (CONF)

2. MIN: 7-2 (OVR), 3-1 (DIV), 5-1 (CONF)

3. CHI: 7-2 (OVR), 0-2 (DIV), 5-2 (CONF)

The win marked Minnesota's second victory over Green Bay this season after opening the year with a 39-22 home win over the Packers in Week 1.

The Vikings moved into second place in the NFC North following the victory. They hold the potential tiebreaker over the Chicago Bears but lost their first matchup against the Detroit Lions by four points, with a rematch scheduled for Week 15.

Minnesota took a commanding 17-0 lead into halftime after a disastrous first quarter by the Packers, who lost a fumble and missed a field goal. Meanwhile, Cousins found Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown.

Green Bay's struggles continued in the second quarter as Love threw an interception, giving the Packers their second turnover of the game.

Aaron Jones Sr. added a rushing touchdown to extend Minnesota's lead to 17 points at halftime, despite Cousins throwing an interception of his own in the quarter.

Despite a fumble on Green Bay's first possession of the second half, the Packers mounted a comeback to cut the deficit to 10 points. Love connected with J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard touchdown before Green Bay added a field goal to trail 20-10 entering the fourth quarter.

Green Bay's costly fourth turnover of the game sealed its fate in the fourth quarter. Cousins found tight end Gavin Bartholomew for a touchdown before an additional field goal extended Minnesota's lead to 20 points, sealing the Vikings' win.

The Vikings will host the San Francisco 49ers next Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET, while the Packers will hit the road to face the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Josh Downs Shines with Mahomes, Chiefs After Trade, Box Score Stats & Highlights vs. Falcons
articles.summary: The Josh Downs era in Kansas City started with a victory.
articles.body:
The Josh Downs era in Kansas City started with a victory.

After acquiring the wide receiver from the Indianapolis Colts via trade, the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 in Sunday's game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Downs wasted no time announcing his presence with a touchdown catch, which helped Patrick Mahomes put on a clinic as the Chiefs improved to 7-2 on the season with a second straight win.

As for the Falcons, they fell to 3-7 with their third consecutive loss and struggled to contain Downs and Emmett Johnson with Mahomes in control.

All eyes were on Downs in his first game with the Chiefs, especially after he and Mahomes had a notable interaction after the trade. The receiver also became all the more important in the aerial attack when tight end Travis Kelce exited with an ankle injury in the first quarter.

Downs hauled in a 21-yard reception in the first quarter and then completely found his footing by the second quarter with a first-down catch in Atlanta territory that helped set up his own touchdown reception in the final minute before halftime.

Kansas City took a 14-3 lead into the locker room in large part because of his presence, as he took advantage of space in the middle of the field when Atlanta was too focused on Rashee Rice and then used his speed and contested-catch ability in the corner of the end zone for the touchdown.

The Chiefs surely envisioned exactly that when they traded for him, especially with Tyquan Thornton sidelined.

It wasn't all Downs, as Johnson filled in admirably for the injured Kenneth Walker III in the backfield. His speed made him a threat every time he touched the ball, and the Chiefs also got him involved in the aerial attack a number of times.

One of those catches went for a touchdown, further stretching the Atlanta defense even before Kelce returned in the second half to give Mahomes another weapon.

The second half was all about the Chiefs pulling away with the defense forcing a turnover on downs to set up a deep ball from Mahomes to Cyrus Allen for a touchdown before Johnson caught another touchdown after a 50-yard reception from Rice.

Atlanta attempted to make a late push with a Bijan Robinson touchdown, recovered onside kick and added a field goal, but it was to no avail as Mahomes put the game away with a long touchdown strike to Andrew Armstrong.

As a result, Kansas City has plenty of momentum heading into a home game against the Arizona Cardinals, while the Falcons will look to turn things around on their bye.

articles.title: Browns Beat Texans After 17-Point Rally, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Watson, Stroud, Top Players
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson engineered another fourth-quarter comeback to lead the Cleveland Browns past his former team, the Houston Texans, by a 27-24 score on Sunday.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson engineered another fourth-quarter comeback to lead the Cleveland Browns past his former team, the Houston Texans, by a 27-24 score on Sunday.

Watson and the Browns erased a 17-point deficit that the Texans opened up in the second quarter to move to 6-4 on the season and 4-0 at home. It's the first time since 1963 that the Browns opened 4-0 at home.

Watson led the Browns on a quick scoring drive to take the lead with less than a minute left in the fourth quarter.

Quinshon Judkins ran in the game-winning touchdown from five yards out.

That score came after Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for a 30-yard completion to get into the red zone.

Judkins' touchdown run was the completion of a come-from-behind effort led by Watson that began in the second quarter.

Watson ran in Cleveland's first touchdown from six yards out to cut the deficit to seven. Andre Szymt hit a 49-yard field goal earlier in the quarter to put the Browns on the board.

Cleveland then tied the game in the middle of the third quarter on a KC Concepcion touchdown run.

The Browns were temporarily in the lead at the end of the third quarter, when Szmyt knocked home a 26-yard field goal.

The Texans responded to the field goal with a touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud to Dalton Schultz.

Stroud produced a pair of touchdown passes in the first half to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson.

The Houston offense was unable to produce one more scoring drive late in the fourth quarter to tie the game.

The Browns didn't allow the Texans to cross midfield on their final drive of the game to seal the victory.

Cleveland won't leave Ohio for the next month. It has a Week 11 bye and then hosts Las Vegas, Cincinnati and Atlanta in a row at home. Houston dropped to 3-6 ahead of a Thursday night home clash with Indianapolis.

articles.title: NFL Week 10 Winners and Losers: Packers and Lions may be in trouble in NFC North race, leaving Vikings and Bears
articles.summary: A key injury to Aidan Hutchinson will have a big impact on the NFC North race.
articles.body:
Before Sunday, the NFC North looked like it would be a four-team battle royal until the end.

Then a freak injury and a home blowout crystallized the race. We might be down to two teams for the division crown.

The Chicago Bears had the week off and they pushed forward a bit because it's hard to buy the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions making much of a move in the division anymore.

The Lions won in Munich early on Sunday but suffered one of the biggest losses of the season when star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson jumped up following a sack to celebrate, and when he came down he suffered a bad knee injury . His "Gramatica" moment is expected to keep him out for a while, via NFL Media . If he's done for the season, the Lions' defense is unlikely to keep the team afloat in the division race.

Detroit is 7-2 and it seems like the season is headed downhill. A defense that was already suspect has to go forward without Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell, who is on injured reserve with a neck injury. It's especially rough that Hutchinson's season might have ended in such a fluky and unnecessary way.

For the Packers, their hot streak came to an abrupt end. The Minnesota Vikings, with Kirk Cousins becoming the first quarterback since 1950 to start for two different teams in back-to-back weeks according to Fox, blew out the Packers 30-10 . The Vikings' defense was stifling yet again, including five sacks in the first half and eight overall. Jordan Love looked like a legitimate MVP candidate before Sunday and now he should fall back to the second tier in that race. The Packers (6-4) are just a game-and-a-half behind the Vikings (7-2) in the standings and there's a chance they could regain momentum when Micah Parsons returns to the lineup, but Sunday's home loss was a huge blow to their chances.

The Lions' major injury and Packers' defeat affected more than the NFC North race. NFC wild-card contenders like the Seahawks and Rams were paying attention too. It's not like the Packers and Lions are dead yet, but their paths to the playoffs got significantly tougher on Sunday.

Perhaps we're already down to the Vikings and Bears in the race. The Vikings looked reborn with Cousins providing competent quarterback play five days after Minnesota's big trade with the Raiders. The Bears' offense has been fine all season and their trade for Jeffery Simmons could transform Chicago's defense in the same way Cousins can lift the Vikings' offense.

The race to win the best division in football got some clarity Sunday. It just wasn't good news in Detroit or Green Bay.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 10 of the NFL season:

Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson: Without Kenneth Walker III on Sunday because of a groin injury, the Chiefs found out some things about their offense.

The first thing they learned was that Johnson, a rookie fifth-round draft pick, took the positive things in a limited role behind Walker and showed he's a legit impact player in his own right. Johnson had a monster game for the Chiefs in a 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons . Johnson had 171 total yards and two receiving touchdowns.

The Chiefs know Mahomes is a star but it was nice to see him have his biggest game of the season. Without Walker, Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns. It was Mahomes' first five-touchdown game since Week 1 of the 2022 season. He found a new weapon in Josh Downs. The Chiefs acquired him in a trade with the Colts on Tuesday and he scored a touchdown Sunday. He could be a nice addition for Kansas City.

The Chiefs are 7-2, and the way they won Sunday without Walker had to be satisfying.

Chuba Hubbard: He has had a very good season for the Carolina Panthers and it got better Sunday.

Hubbard had a career high with 172 total yards from scrimmage and came through when the Panthers needed it most. Trailing 14-10, Hubbard had a 34-yard catch to set up his 1-yard touchdown run with 1:49 left to give Carolina the lead. After the Saints tied it with a field goal, the Panthers got a quick big play on a pass interference call on a deep pass to Jalen Coker, setting up their own field-goal attempt. Ryan Fitzgerald nailed it from 54 yards as time expired and the Panthers won 20-17 .

The Panthers are just 4-5 but right in the mix for the NFC South title. Hubbard has been a big part of those Panthers wins, and he had his best game Sunday.

Post-deadline Jacksonville Jaguars: The Jaguars knew they were in good shape to beat the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. So they decided to give big deadline acquisitions defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III the week off to help rest and acclimate to their new team.

That gamble worked. The Jaguars won without those two defensive standouts, beating the Titans 40-23 . Trevor Lawrence was fantastic with 352 yards and three touchdowns. The defense wasn't great, but it will get Davis and Bates in the lineup next week vs. the Giants and will improve immediately. The defense has been pretty good before Sunday too.

The Jaguars are a complete team and a Super Bowl contender. And it should get only better from here.

DeMeco Ryans and the Houston Texans' defense: Houston was supposed to have one of the best defenses in the NFL this season. It hasn't been, and on Sunday it was a big reason the Texans took a loss that is a huge blow to their playoff hopes.

The Texans allowed a game-winning drive to the Cleveland Browns in the final two minutes, with Quinshon Judkins scoring the go-ahead touchdown with 53 seconds left on a 5-yard run. The Browns' defense, which was excellent in the fourth quarter, held after that to clinch the 27-24 win .

The Texans were without a few key players because of injuries. They will argue, rightfully, that a huge unnecessary roughness penalty on cornerback Kwame Lassiter was just a defensive back going for the ball and the hit on the intended receiver wasn't worthy of a flag. It doesn't matter. The Texans are 3-6 and surprisingly, Ryans' defense is a major reason for that disappointing record.

Geno Smith: It has been a rough season for the New York Jets and Smith, and for the quarterback it got even worse.

Smith took a massive hit against the Buffalo Bills and even though he was cleared in the concussion protocol he was later ruled out with an ankle injury. The Jets had been playing well but Cade Klubnik couldn't keep the team in the game and New York lost to the Buffalo Bills 31-12 .

The Jets (2-8) have won only once since Week 1. Smith, who was a short-term answer at quarterback anyway, could get pushed out of the starting spot for the rookie Klubnik soon, if it doesn't happen next week against the Chargers.

It's not like winning games is a high priority for the Jets the rest of the season. Smith got injured Sunday and the news might continue to get worse for him.

Kyle McCord: He did the best he could. Even against the Indianapolis Colts, it was asking a lot for a 2025 sixth-round draft pick taking his first NFL snaps to run a competent offense given Miami's supporting cast.

McCord helped the Miami Dolphins stay in the game. But trailing by two points late, he took a third-down sack with the Dolphins just outside of field-goal range. His fourth-down pass was batted down and the Colts survived with a 24-22 win . McCord was better than Daniel Jones, who was awful again. The Dolphins QB had 209 passing yards, almost double the 108 that Jones put up. He also had a rushing touchdown. But McCord couldn't get the play he needed at the end, and his fumble that was recovered in the end zone for a Colts touchdown was a big difference in the final.

McCord will get more chances with Malik Willis on injured reserve for at least three more games. His first effort wasn't bad, it just wasn't good enough for the win.

NFL fans in Germany: The NFL tried to give its German fans a good matchup. The New England Patriots vs. the Detroit Lions was a fun one, until one sack at the end of the Patriots' first drive.

Quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on a sack (which was a borderline hip drop tackle) by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, then Hutchinson suffered a knee injury celebrating. That took out two of the biggest stars in the game. The Patriots' offense, with Tommy DeVito at quarterback, was unwatchable after that. New England, with Maye, had 60 yards on the opening drive and 91 on the 11 drives after that in a 35-10 loss .

There were some things for German fans to cheer. Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose mother is German and carried the country's flag onto the field during pregame introductions, had two fun touchdowns.

Jahmyr Gibbs' brilliance was on full display with 153 yards rushing, 99 yards receiving and two touchdowns. There were some highlights. But it was an ugly game after Maye left it due to injury.

articles.title: Ed Kelce’s love and sacrifices shaped Jason and Travis Kelce’s NFL journey, but his greatest legacy lies in the love that held their family together
articles.summary: Behind NFL stars Jason and Travis Kelce’s success is a father who spent years making sure they had the support to follow their dreams.
articles.body: Behind NFL stars Jason and Travis Kelce’s success is a father who spent years making sure they had the support to follow their dreams. Ed Kelce coached them, encouraged their love for sports and made personal sacrifices to give them better opportunities. Even when his marriage with Donna Kelce faced difficulties, he continued putting his sons first. His journey shows how much a parent’s support can matter in a child’s life.How Ed Kelce helped Jason and Travis Kelce discover their love for sportsEd Kelce grew up in Cleveland, Ohio, where he developed an interest in football and baseball. Having played both sports himself, he understood how much they could teach children. When Jason and Travis were young, he wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path.He started getting involved when the boys were very little. Ed coached Travis in T-ball and Jason in coach-pitch baseball. He also spent time playing with them in the front yard and created space in the family garage where they could practise.One of his favourite memories goes back to when Jason was still a toddler. His son would roll a ball towards him on the living-room floor, and Ed would roll it back. It was a simple activity, but it became one of their earliest shared memories.Years later, while appearing on the brothers’ New Heights podcast, Ed explained how he viewed his responsibility as a father.“My job is to help you find a passion, and then feed that passion. Whatever you want to do, I’m there.”He wanted both boys to discover what they enjoyed and then work towards becoming better at it. He also believed that talent needed to be supported by hard work. Rather than always placing them in situations where they could easily succeed, he encouraged them to compete and learn from more difficult experiences.That approach helped Jason and Travis develop their interest in football. Both eventually attended the University of Cincinnati, where they played college football before entering the NFL.The sacrifices Ed and Donna Kelce made to support their sonsRaising two children with serious sporting ambitions required time, money and a lot of planning. Jason and Travis played different sports and had busy schedules, so their parents had to manage practices, competitions, travel and equipment costs.Ed worked in the steel industry before moving into sales, while Donna built her career in banking. Both had professional responsibilities, but they made sure their sons received the support they needed.The financial side was not always easy. The family had to plan its spending around the boys’ sporting activities, including equipment, travel and other expenses. Ed and Donna had to make choices to ensure both children could take part in the activities they enjoyed.They also divided their parenting responsibilities carefully. Donna explained on New Heights that they worked as a team. When one parent travelled with Jason for a game, the other stayed home with Travis. This allowed both boys to receive attention and support, even when their schedules clashed.Donna described their arrangement as being “like a tag team with you two.”It was not always possible for both parents to attend every event, but they made sure someone was there. Their priority was to give Jason and Travis equal opportunities rather than allowing one child’s sporting commitments to take over family life.Neither Ed nor Donna knew that their sons would eventually become NFL stars. They were simply making sure the boys had the chance to explore their interests and work towards their goals.How Ed Kelce and Donna Kelce put their children first despite marriage problemsWhile Ed and Donna were busy raising their sons, their own marriage was going through a difficult period. The couple had been married for nearly 25 years, but their relationship was not always happy.Travis spoke about this in the Prime Video documentary Kelce. He remembered noticing during childhood that his parents did not share a bedroom. As he reached middle school, he began to understand that their marriage was struggling.Despite their personal problems, Ed and Donna continued raising their sons together. They knew that separating while Jason and Travis were still studying and playing sports would make an already busy family life more difficult.Ed explained their decision in the documentary, saying, “If we had split as we probably both would have preferred, that would have been a nightmare with the logistics, getting kids where they had to be and providing all the support.”His words give an idea of the practical challenges they were trying to avoid. They had to manage school, sports, travel and other family responsibilities, and both understood how much their sons depended on them.Their marriage eventually ended in divorce after Jason and Travis had graduated from college. However, their separation did not end their responsibilities as parents. They continued to support their sons and remained connected as a family.Donna has also spoken warmly about Ed and their years together, making it clear that she does not regret the family they built.Ed Kelce never stopped supporting Jason and Travis after their NFL successEd’s involvement did not end when his sons left home for college. When Jason joined the Philadelphia Eagles and Travis became a star with the Kansas City Chiefs, he continued attending games and following their careers.Supporting both sons became more challenging once they started playing for different NFL teams. Their games were often held in different cities, making it difficult for Ed and Donna to be present at every match. They continued dividing their time so both brothers could receive support.One of the most memorable moments came during Super Bowl LVII in February 2023, when Jason’s Eagles faced Travis’s Chiefs. It was an unusual situation for the family because one son would celebrate winning the championship while the other would have to deal with defeat.Ed understood how difficult that could be. Before the game, he explained that he wanted to be with whichever son lost.“Somebody’s gonna feel pretty crummy and I wanna be with him-initially.”He also joked that he had already won because both his sons had reached the Super Bowl.The game ended with Travis and the Chiefs defeating Jason and the Eagles 38-35. Ed and Donna celebrated with Travis but also had to share the difficult moment with Jason.For Ed, the journey was about much more than watching his sons become famous football players. He had been there when they first started playing sports, helped them through their childhood and continued supporting them when their careers reached the highest level.His story is a reminder that behind many successful athletes are parents who make sacrifices without knowing where their children’s dreams will eventually lead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bills' Josh Allen Hypes James Cook After RB Keeps TD Streak Alive with 74-Yard Score vs. Jets
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen led his team to a fifth straight victory Sunday with a 31-12 win over the New York Jets, but he certainly had some help.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen led his team to a fifth straight victory Sunday with a 31-12 win over the New York Jets, but he certainly had some help.

Running back James Cook III ran for 157 yards and a touchdown, which was from 74 yards out and all but put the game away. Cook earned some praise from Allen in the process, who called the running back "our workhorse," after notching a touchdown in his eighth straight games.

Buffalo looks the part of a Super Bowl contender at 8-1, and Allen's impact was once again felt in addition to Cook even though he threw for just 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

After all, Allen ran for two touchdowns and created some much-needed breathing room with a long strike to DJ Moore late in the third quarter.

New York, which played both Geno Smith and Cade Klubnik under center with the former exiting with injury, was down just five late in the third quarter thanks to four field goals from Jason Sanders.

However, the Moore touchdown strike created separation Buffalo never relinquished, and Cook added an exclamation point near the end with his long touchdown run.

It was more of the same for Allen, who is is a four-time Pro Bowler and took home the NFL MVP Award in 2024. He also accounted for 39 or more total touchdowns in six straight seasons from 2020 to 2025.

His five straight seasons with 40 or more passing, rushing and receiving touchdowns from 2020 to 2024 is an NFL record.

The one knock against Allen is that he has yet to lead the Bills to the Super Bowl during his career, but he has been among the best playoff-performing quarterbacks of all time despite that.

In 15 career postseason starts, Allen has completed 66.5 percent of his passes for 3,915 yards, 29 touchdowns and six interceptions, while also rushing for 767 yards and nine scores.

With Allen leading the way, the Bills have made seven consecutive playoff appearances, and they won five straight AFC East titles from 2020 to 2024.

They seem well on their way to another divisional crown this season thanks to a red-hot start.

Minnesota traded to get Kirk Cousins back in the purple and yellow, and the deal paid off Sunday.

The Vikings dominated the Packers in a high-stakes division match-up in Green Bay, with the defense tallying eight sacks of quarterback Jordan Love and intercepting him once.

With Cousins under center, the Vikings offense appeared more effective and efficient, with the veteran quarterback completing 21-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns.

Justin Jefferson caught nine balls for 74 yards, and three other receivers recorded double-digit yardage.

The Vikings have the best defense in the league and now a tenured quarterback who has proven himself in the offense before.

With a dominant win over the Packers, Minnesota looks the part of a Super Bowl contender. Whether they can avoid some of the mistakes that have plagued Cousins throughout his career, particularly in big-game situations, will determine whether or not the purple and gold will return to the Super Bowl for the first time since 1977.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza's first NFL TD comes on designed run reminiscent of his iconic score that sealed Indiana's national championship
articles.summary: So far, so good for starting  NFL quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
articles.body:
So far, so good for starting NFL quarterback Fernando Mendoza.

With Kirk Cousins playing and winning with the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, the Mendoza era officially began in Las Vegas as the rookie quarterback made his first NFL start.

It began with reason for celebration on Las Vegas' first possession of the game against the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks.

Mendoza began his first NFL possession in good field position after a Seahawks fumble. He finished it 46 yards later with a 10-yard touchdown run for his first NFL score and a 7-0 Raiders lead.

Mendoza also completed all three of his first-possession passes for 20 yards before keeping the ball on a designed draw for the score.

The play was reminiscent of the touchdown Mendoza scored to cap Indiana's College Football Championship game win over Miami last season.

The Raiders used the No. 1 pick in the NFL Draft to select Mendoza after his Heisman Trophy-winning and national championship campaign. Save a brief appearance in a Week 5 loss to the Patriots, he spent his first eight NFL weeks learning from the bench with tutelage from Cousins.

But the Vikings traded for Cousins ahead of the trade deadline, starting the Mendoza era in earnest. And with the Super Bowl champions in town, Mendoza didn't blink on his first possession as an NFL starter.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Gets Emotional Discussing 1st Win Back with Vikings After Trade in Trending Video
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins' return to Minnesota couldn't have gone much better.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins' return to Minnesota couldn't have gone much better.

Just days after being traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in his team's 30-10 statement win over the Green Bay Packers.

After the game, Cousins spoke about the performance and being back with the Vikings.

Vikings Dominate Packers in Kirk's Return

"It was emotional coming to [Lambeau Field]," he told ESPN's Lindsey Thiry. "Three years ago tearing my Achilles here, it's been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today. Grateful for my teammates today for what they did to make this outcome possible."

He also credited a defense that forced four turnovers and sacked Jordan Love eight times.

"There's gonna be a lot of talk about offense and my addition here, but it's the defense," he told Fox Sports' Kristina Pink. "The defense just played lights out, kept giving us the ball back. Thought our staff did a great job putting together a plan to allow me to be comfortable. My teammates made plays and took it off my shoulders. It's a fun day to get a win."

There were plenty of promising aspects of Cousins' return, but perhaps none was bigger than this—superstar wideout Justin Jefferson was targeted 13 times, pulling down nine catches for 74 yards. Jefferson had clearly grown frustrated with the team's rough quarterback play this season, but his his best seasons came with Cousins and that connection was still alive and well on Sunday.

Because of the team's defense and the playmakers it has on offense, it felt like the Vikings (7-2) were just better quarterback play away from being legitimate contenders. Consider Sunday proof of concept.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Reacts to Texans Blowing 17-0 Lead vs. Browns to Fall to 3-6, 'Time Is Running Out'
articles.summary: The Houston Texans scored on their first three drives against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, taking a 17-0 lead early in the second quarter.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans scored on their first three drives against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, taking a 17-0 lead early in the second quarter.

But it was almost all Browns from there, as Cleveland erased the deficit and ultimately beat the Texans 27-24, dropping them to 3-6 in the process. It was another blow to Houston's rapidly-dimming playoff hopes.

"The time is now and time is running out," Texans' quarterback C.J. Stroud told reporters following the loss.

Much of this loss falls on the offense. Houston started the second half with four straight three-and-outs and had six three-and-outs in eight total second-half drives.

But it wasn't just the offense. The Texans were penalized 13 times. The defense gave up 312 yards through the air to Deshaun Watson and allowed the Browns to convert nearly half of third downs (7-for-15). The Texans have seemed to find ways to lose this season, and Sunday was another example.

Five of Houston's six losses this season have been by a touchdown or less. In four of those losses, a once-vaunted defense has given up 27 or more points. And it's come while C.J. Stroud is having an excellent season (19 touchdowns, three interceptions), answering many of the questions that dogged him in recent seasons and limited Houston's upside.

At this point, the Texans may need to win out to reach the postseason. At the very least, it will probably take 10 wins, and while the schedule is manageable, there are still tough matchups against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Pittsburgh Steelers and Green Bay Packers to come.

Houston is indeed running low on time to salvage the season.

articles.title: Jets' Geno Smith crushed on a massive hit, leads to concussion protocol on injury-filled day

articles.body: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith had an injury-filled Sunday against the Buffalo Bills that saw a brief exit, his return and then an absence for good in the 31-12 loss to their AFC East foe. The first injury that occurred came late in the second quarter when the veteran signal caller was trying to make a pass. After one possession led by Klubnik, Smith was seen on the field again, but he had to leave the game due to an ankle injury this time. It’s unknown what play exactly landed Smith out again, but he was seen walking to the locker room as the game started to get out of reach in the fourth quarter. Smith was 13-of-21 for 148 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions in the loss. Meanwhile, Klubnik, a fourth-round pick out of Clemson, went 11-of-20 with one interception and no touchdowns after coming in for Smith. With the loss, the Jets have now dropped five straight games, moving to a paltry 2-8 on the season.
