articles.title: Rams star Aaron Donald records first sack since coming out of retirement in game vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Aaron Donald got his first sack in 1,050 days on Sunday afternoon at State Farm Stadium.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald, for the first time in nearly three years, has sacked a quarterback.

The Los Angeles Rams star, who came out of retirement earlier this fall to rejoin the franchise, brought down Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck early in the second quarter of their matchup on Sunday afternoon. It marked his first sack since Dec. 31, 2023, or 1,050 days ago.

The sack forced a fourth down, and got the Rams the ball back in the contest at State Farm Stadium.

Donald retired shortly after his final sack in 2023. He finished with 53 total tackles and eight sacks in that campaign. Earlier this fall, after rumors for weeks, Donald rejoined the Rams to team up with fellow defensive star Myles Garrett and bolster the Rams' chances at making a deep postseason run.

The 35-year-old made his debut on Sept. 21 in a win over the New York Giants, and had three tackles in that contest. While he's been impressive in his return, especially considering he had been away from the game for so long, Donald failed to record a sack in his first seven games this fall. Donald entered Sunday's contest with 13 total tackles, including seven solo.

The sack on Sunday marked the 112th of his career. That's good for 42nd on the league's all-time list. While he's well back from the 200 that leader Bruce Smith recorded in his career, there are only seven active players in the NFL with more sacks than Donald.

The Rams, who will have a bye next week, carried a 5-4 record into Sunday's game in Arizona. They've won three straight, however, and finally got above .500 for the first time all season with their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders last week.

Though the Rams still have a long way to go to actually make a run at another ring, Donald finally getting his first sack out of the way is a big step for him in his comeback.

articles.title: The biggest move of the NFL trade deadline paid immediate dividends
articles.summary: Making his first start for the Minnesota Vikings since 2023, quarterback Kirk Cousins picked up where he left off — almost literally.
articles.body: Making his first start for the Minnesota Vikings since 2023, quarterback Kirk Cousins picked up where he left off — almost literally. Cousins led the Vikings to a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, ending Minnesota’s two-game losing streak and improving the team’s record to 7-2. Cousins’s most recent start for the Vikings prior to Sunday also came at Green Bay. It was in 2023, and he tore his Achilles during that game, and Minnesota moved on from him the following offseason. The Vikings have been looking for an answer at quarterback since, and they eventually came back around to Cousins at this year’s trade deadline. Cousins got the start Sunday only five days after he was acquired from the Las Vegas Raiders, and he made some big throws as he led Minnesota to its highest scoring output since Week 1. “I didn’t even know what my code was to get into the building on Wednesday,” Cousins said postgame. “It took a village. I’m just grateful for all the people that stepped up to help.” Cousins finished the game completing 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception. While his stats weren’t spectacular, he made a meaningful impact on money downs, as the Vikings finished the game converting eight of 16 on third down. (Entering Sunday, Minnesota was ranked 30th in third-down conversion percentage at 33.3%.) Minnesota’s first touchdown came on a third and 23, as Cousins made a beautiful, drop-in-the-bucket throw to Myles Price, who bounced off defenders en route to the end zone. Cousins described it as a “big-time” play by Price. Cousins made another great throw on a third-and-long later in the game, connecting with Tai Felton on a wheel route on a third and 15 in the second quarter. The pass set up a one-yard touchdown run on the next play. Later, after the Packers had cut the Vikings’ 20-0 lead to 20-10, Cousins picked up another massive first, checking into a screen pass on third and 12 and finding Justin Jefferson for a first down. “It was fun, it felt like old times watching Justin do what he just did on that play,” Cousins said. “It was like, ‘I remember that guy. He’s pretty special.’” Five plays later, Cousins threw his second touchdown of the game and effectively iced any chances of a Green Bay comeback. “[He] just brought a certain amount of poise, leadership, execution,” head coach Kevin O’Connell said postgame. “Ran the show incredibly clean. Can’t say enough about him, I know everybody in the organization felt it this week.” Jefferson, one of the game’s top receivers, was perhaps the biggest individual beneficiary of his old quarterback’s return. Jefferson’s nine receptions and 13 targets were both season highs. Though Cousins didn’t exactly light the box score on fire, his presence Sunday made Minnesota’s championship formula incredibly clear: Play lights out defense, and do just enough on offense with above-average quarterback play. With Cousins helping push the Vikings out to an early lead, Minnesota’s defense pinned its ears back and got after Jordan Love. The Vikings finished the game with eight sacks, and limited the Packers to only 56 yards rushing. Love, one of the game’s great deep-ball throwers, finished the game with 220 yards, his fewest since Week 4. His 46.6 QBR was also his third-worst mark of the season. “For one of the first times this year, I thought we played complementary football,” O’Connell said. The win was an important one for Minnesota. The Vikings are now two games clear of Green Bay in loss column in the loaded NFC North, and now also own the tiebreaker between the two teams. Minnesota kept pace with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, both of whom are also 7-2. The Vikings’ offense didn’t necessarily look perfect Sunday. But their quarterback making big throws and providing a steady hand while the defensedefense continued to dominate showed exactly why Minnesota decided to bring Cousins back.

articles.title: Rex Ryan's Nashville arrest sparks questions as ESPN confirms NFL analyst will return despite six misdemeanor charges
articles.summary: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan appeared on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown on November 15, just four days after turning himself in to Nashville police over an
articles.body: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan appeared on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown on November 15, just four days after turning himself in to Nashville police over an alleged incident involving two pedestrians. ESPN had confirmed that Ryan would continue with his scheduled television duties despite the six misdemeanor charges he faces. The 63-year-old analyst did return to the programme, making his first public appearance since his arrest. However, Ryan kept his comments focused on football and did not address the allegations during the broadcast. His appearance came as questions continued over the Nashville case.Rex Ryan faces six misdemeanor charges after alleged Nashville road incidentRyan surrendered to police on Wednesday, November 11, after authorities issued six misdemeanor warrants against him. The case relates to an incident shortly before midnight on November 5, when his pickup truck allegedly struck two pedestrians crossing Broadway in downtown Nashville.According to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department, the two people were crossing from Fourth Avenue with a walk signal when Ryan allegedly turned right in his truck. Police said the vehicle ran over both pedestrians’ feet and also made contact with one person’s leg.The police account states that the truck continued moving before stopping at a red light near Broadway and Representative John Lewis Way. The pedestrians reportedly approached the driver and tried to get his attention. Police said, “They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away.”The two pedestrians then took photographs of the truck’s licence plate and the driver, which helped investigators identify Ryan, according to police.Ryan now faces two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information or render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal. His bond was set at $6,000, and he was released from custody on Wednesday.The allegations have not been proven in court. Ryan’s attorney has said that he surrendered after learning about the allegations and would cooperate with authorities. His next court appearance is scheduled for December 18.ESPN confirms Rex Ryan’s Sunday NFL Countdown return despite arrestRyan’s television future became a talking point after news of his arrest emerged. However, ESPN made clear that he would not miss his scheduled appearance on the network’s popular NFL pregame programme.A spokesperson for ESPN told reporters on Saturday, November 14, “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.”The statement confirmed that the network had no immediate plans to take Ryan off its Sunday programme while the legal case remained ongoing. The Athletic’s Richard Deitsch also shared the network’s position ahead of the broadcast.Ryan appeared on the show on Sunday, November 15, alongside the programme’s regular coverage team. Rather than discussing the arrest, he stayed with the football discussion and did not publicly respond to the allegations during the appearance.The former coach has been part of ESPN’s NFL coverage since 2017, following his coaching career with the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. His time with the Jets included back-to-back appearances in the AFC Championship Game after the 2009 and 2010 seasons.For now, Ryan has returned to his regular television duties, while the legal proceedings over the Nashville incident are still ahead.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kirk Cousins kept repeating what the Vikings brought him to do in postgame interview
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins isn't fooling himself. He understands exactly why the Vikings brought him back.
articles.body:
Everyone knows why the Minnesota Vikings made a bold trade to reacquire Kirk Cousins . They think that even an average offense with solid enough quarterback play is enough to contend for the Super Bowl in February. After the Cousins-led Vikings humbled the Green Bay Packers 30-10 on Sunday, the emotional veteran made it clear that he also understands this important distinction. Better than anyone, he knows his role at this stage of his career.

Again, Cousins is back in Minnesota to make enough plays for Minnesota's functional offense so its dominant defense can close the deal without a rusty anchor dragging it down. Every Sunday. Nothing more. Nothing less. There's no need to dance around the obvious.

The 38-year-old Cousins kept repeating this sentiment during his postgame interview with Fox's Kristina Pink. He's an experienced caretaker capable of making occasional big throws. It is the Vikings' defense that can ultimately take them as far as they want:

In a one-game sample size, the Vikings' new grand gambit with Cousins looked like it would pay off with flying colors. We'll see how Cousins and Co. maintain this strategy moving forward. Something tells me that, at the very least, their offense will hold up their end of the bargain.

articles.title: Matt LaFleur Says Packers Got 'Humbled' After 'Butt-Whooping' by Kirk Cousins, Vikings
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers suffered a 30-10 loss against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Lambeau Field. After the game, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged the lopsided nature of the game.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers suffered a 30-10 loss against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Lambeau Field. After the game, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged the lopsided nature of the game.

"That was a butt-whooping today," LaFleur said. "This is a humbling league, and today we got humbled. I think they're a really good football team, and any time you spot them and turn the ball over four times to their one, that's a recipe for disaster. Give them credit, they do a great job, but obviously we didn't coach well enough and certainly we didn't go out there and execute well enough."

Vikings Dominate Packers in Kirk's Return

The Packers entered the game with high morale after they trounced the New England Patriots last week. Green Bay scored 45 points in that game — the most points scored by any visiting team at Gillette Stadium. After the strong performance, quarterback Jordan Love was tied for the fourth-best odds to win the AP NFL Most Valuable Player award at FanDuel Sportsbook, per The Athletic's Matt Schneidman .

Minnesota's defense has humbled offenses all season long, and Sunday's performance was no exception. Love was sacked eight times and finished with just 220 passing yards with a touchdown and an interception. Green Bay was held scoreless through the first half and fumbled three times — each of which resulted in a field goal for the Vikings.

At 7-2, the Vikings are in a three-way tie for the top spot in the NFC North. The Packers, who entered the game in last place, will have an even tougher path to a division title after falling to a 6-4 record.

articles.title: Xavier Smith scores first NFL TD after Rams steal him from 49ers
articles.summary: In his first game back with the Rams, Xavier Smith found the end zone on a 22-yard screen pass – his first career touchdown in the NFL.
articles.body:
Welcome back, Xavier Smith. The Los Angeles Rams brought him back this past week by signing him off the San Francisco 49ers' practice squad, and he made the most of his return on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals .

In the second quarter, he found the end zone for his first career touchdown, a 22-yard catch-and-run on a screen pass from Matthew Stafford. It was a perfectly executed play, as Smith sprinted upfield and followed his blockers before evading one tackler on his way to the end zone.

Smith has been criticized often by fans throughout his time with the Rams, primarily because of his struggles on special teams. But as an offensive player, his speed is a weapon for Los Angeles, and it showed on this play.

articles.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers leaves game vs. Seahawks early with ankle injury
articles.summary: Brock Bowers went down awkwardly in a pile early on Sunday afternoon in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Brock Bowers didn't last long on Sunday afternoon.

The Las Vegas Raiders tight end was ruled out of their game against the Seattle Seahawks due to an ankle injury he suffered early in the first quarter. That knocked him out for the majority of Fernando Mendoza's starting debut at Allegiant Stadium .

Bowers, in the first quarter of the contest, went up to block Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori for running back Ashton Jeanty. But as Jeanty cut the other way, Bowers had his legs rolled up on in a pile and he went down awkwardly.

Bowers remained down for a few moments while the team's training staff helped him, and he then limped to the sideline.

Bowers did return to the game briefly after that, which helped lead the way for Mendoza's rushing touchdown to get them on the board. But he left the game again late in the second quarter, and the team ruled him out for good just before the start of the second half with the ankle injury. Clearly, it was just too much for him to overcome.

Further specifics of his injury are not yet known. Bowers finished with two catches for 18 yards. He entered Sunday with 658 yards and six touchdowns this season, his third in the league after the Raiders took him with the No. 13 overall pick out of Georgia in 2024.

The Raiders, who dealt away quarterback Kirk Cousins at the deadline, entered Sunday's contest with a 4-5 record. The trade paved the way for Mendoza, the former Indiana star and reigning Heisman Trophy winner, to get the first start of his career.

Though Mendoza appears to be holding his own so far, losing a target like Bowers for any substantial amount of time will make things much more difficult for him as his NFL career gets going.
